data.narrative:
44.01 is a Series A-stage climate and energy company that has raised $37M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine frontier-tech energy companies—one public (Lnza) and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix—though tight stage and tier filters limit direct peer comparability.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised as a proxy anchor ($37M) and applying a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to subsequent rounds yields an implied valuation of $74M. A Peer-Median triangulation was not viable; while eight same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters for stage, adjacent-stage, and valuation tier produced insufficient overlap (fewer than three datapoints required). Broader cross-sector comparison would introduce material noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $63M to $85M, centered on $74M. This single-method result carries elevated uncertainty. Key sensitivities include the magnitude of the Series A step-up multiplier, which can range between 1.5x and 2.5x depending on capital efficiency, market conditions, and technology validation milestones. Additionally, the absence of tight peer comparables leaves sector-specific risk factors—regulatory, technical, and commercialization timing—inadequately benchmarked.
